nodes.label: Finite foreign-residue projection reduction
nodes.statement: The finite Möbius residue diagonal splits exactly into projected foreign and divisor channels, and every finite stable tail window has a closed geometric bound. If an analytic kernel/complement bridge controls the actual foreign defect by that bound and the projection is separated from every integer, then the full target is missed. The analytic bridge and any unbounded separated-projection supply are not proved.

nodes.label: Scalar-localisation height obstruction
nodes.statement: If H divides the reduced denominator of a rational x and the reduced denominator of c·x divides H for an integer c, then the complementary factor x.den/H divides |c|. Scalar localisation transfers, rather than discards, that denominator information; this local obstruction is not an irrationality criterion.

nodes.label: Adjacent-pair phase separation reduction
nodes.statement: At scales satisfying the explicit dyadic room inequality, a squared chordal separation of at least 19/25 between two adjacent first-harmonic phases in a dyadic block forces a certified non-integrality witness at one of the two indices. A cofinal supply of such adjacent pairs implies irrationality of the totient constant; no such supply is proved.

nodes.label: Affine residue state and old-channel annihilation
nodes.statement: The exact Möbius residue kernel has a periodic affine slope-and-intercept state. First-order exponent transport and every coefficient system with vanishing zeroth and first moments annihilate all divisor channels already present at the base height; a prime jump additionally has an explicit migrated-channel correction.

nodes.label: All-base totient-kernel reduction, spanning, and conditional rank
nodes.statement: For every integer base k at least 2, Lean checks the zero-residue scaling identity, the exact nonzero scalar used in composite-base residue reduction, unique quotient/nonzero-digit coordinates, and cardinality k^e + 1 of the canonical finite-level index. It proves unconditionally that this canonical family spans the complete kernel through level e, and proves exact rank k^e + 1 under the explicit hypothesis that the family is linearly independent. Lean does not prove that hypothesis or formalise Martin's positive-density theorem; the unconditional basis and rank theorem in the paper uses Martin externally.

nodes.label: Boolean–Möbius carry certificate equivalence
nodes.statement: A nonempty normalised support, one omitting 0, with series value p/q exists exactly when a positive, square-root-bounded integer orbit with Boolean Möbius quotient exists; the support is reconstructed from the certificate.

nodes.label: Boundary-pulse normalization at the largest-skip crossing
nodes.statement: The row-s pulse of a selected rank e contributes two when e divides 2s+1 and one when e divides 2s+2. For a largest skip d with 2s < 3d, every filled suffix rank d < e < s divides neither index, so the word pulse is exactly the selected-prefix pulse below d. At the first crossing 2s < 3d <= 2(s+1), either 3d = 2s+1 with pulse two or 3d = 2s+2 with pulse one. The transition-carry estimate that would use these exact counts is not proved.

nodes.label: Campbell shift-synchronization strategy boundary
nodes.statement: Campbell's application of the Alford-Granville-Pomerance estimate chooses delta = 1/4, so at prime-search height X the progression modulus d must satisfy d <= X^(1/4), equivalently d^4 <= X. In the proposed last-skip synchronization, P is the fatal-window prime cap, t the unavoidable phase period, and d the combined progression modulus. Taking X = P, the requirements 2 <= d, t <= d, P <= 4t, and d^4 <= P are inconsistent. The shifted-zero interface is guarded by a putative last skip and is exactly equivalent to infinitely many actual greedy skips and to membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set. It is an endpoint restatement, not an independent Campbell input, and proves no half-membership.

nodes.label: Canonical strict-jump slack reduction
nodes.statement: The two canonical adjacent-suffix central-band inequalities are equivalent to nonnegativity of one explicit integer slack. Cofinal nonnegative slack at strict lcm jumps implies irrationality of the totient constant; that cofinal sign statement remains open.

nodes.label: Certificate completeness
nodes.statement: At fixed parameters, a certified kill exists exactly when the corresponding tail difference is non-integral. At every positive shift, integrality of one tail difference forces S to be rational; thus irrationality is equivalent to pointwise non-integrality, and to pointwise finite certificates.

nodes.label: Exact reduction of #249 to finite decidable certificates
nodes.statement: S is irrational if and only if certified non-integrality witnesses occur at unbounded parameters. The pointwise completeness theorem and the diagonal supply theorem together show that an unbounded lcm-diagonal supply is equivalent as well. Producing that supply remains open.

nodes.label: Initial certified-kill segment and generated certificates
nodes.statement: Kernel-checked certified kills for the listed small periods, every lcm-diagonal scale t ≤ 82, and the finite certificate shards. The historical 28 explicit deposits through t = 64 form a strict subset of this contiguous finite band.

nodes.label: Cofinal square-root-strip return closure
nodes.statement: The binary-scaled uncentred greedy half carry is antitone, and the square-root strip envelope divided by 2^N tends to zero. Therefore cofinal returns of the canonical greedy carry to that strip force the scaled carry to tend to zero and yield membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set. The cofinal return hypothesis is not proved.

nodes.label: Composite dilation defect identity
nodes.statement: For every positive support element a and positive x, the divisor-count coefficient at a·x is the coefficient at x, plus the distinguished new divisor when a does not divide x, plus an exact finite composite-dilation defect. For a finite-core orthogonal-petal bouquet, the ray defect is bounded by the finite exceptional-frame cardinality plus the petal-support divisor count. This local identity supplies no correlation estimate, tail selector, or irrationality theorem.

nodes.label: Concrete adjacent-cut producer-carry coordinates
nodes.statement: For every adjacent cut at rank s ≥ 5, the below and above words are the neighbouring subset sums bracketing the target; their remainder and overshoot are the unsigned distances, and their pulses are the paired divisor-incidence contributions of the next two rows. After adjoining terminal rank s, the below producer carry is 4 times the remainder minus the below pulse minus 4, while the above producer carry is the negative of 4 times the overshoot plus the above pulse plus 4. Hence the upper carry is negative and the middle sign depends on the remainder-pulse competition. These exact identities supply no uniform exponential lower bound, sign persistence at unbounded ranks, or universal escape argument.

nodes.label: Concrete finite seam adapter
nodes.statement: Concrete finite seam words realize the abstract adjacent-cut recurrence, and the next seam word agrees with the integer-greedy choice. This implements the finite recurrence but does not establish the unbounded remainder estimate.

nodes.label: Unconditional denominator exclusion for the totient constant
nodes.statement: S = ∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ is not equal to p/q for any integer p and any 1 ≤ q ≤ 79 639 646 646 701 375 323 355 774 875 831 053 (≈ 7.96 × 10³⁴). A lower bound on any rational representation, not a proof of irrationality.

nodes.label: Fresh-loss projection and suffix-supply reduction
nodes.statement: The fresh-loss residue certificate is exactly an integer projection inequality, and such a projection forces full-target avoidance. An unbounded projection supply—or the stronger adjacent-suffix gap supplies formalised here—implies irrationality; no unbounded supply is asserted.

nodes.label: Exact full-target reduction on the lcm diagonal
nodes.statement: At each lcm-diagonal scale, integrality is equivalent to a foreign-defect term landing in an explicit full-target interval. Globally, S is irrational if and only if the full target is avoided at arbitrarily large diagonal scales; that cofinal avoidance is not proved.

nodes.label: T64 diagonal-pincer endpoint certificate
nodes.statement: Lean checks the diagonal-pincer certified kill at t = 64 using the committed T64 Lucas-primality closure. This is one finite certificate and does not assert an unbounded certificate supply or irrationality.

nodes.label: T64 diagonal-pincer primality closure
nodes.statement: A generated proof-producing Lucas-certificate module supplies the primality dependencies for the t=47,49,53,59,61,64 diagonal-pincer certificates. This is finite certificate infrastructure; it neither supplies an unbounded certificate family nor proves irrationality.

nodes.label: Dyadic-prefix, block-safety, and primitive-overshoot interfaces
nodes.statement: Inside a hypothetical dyadic-rational support value, a reduced finite positive prefix transports exactly to a residual rational support value and wrap-ratio certificate. For the half-greedy orbit, reduced and raw margins, three-depth take-run excess, primitive-lattice cap violation, support-coefficient tail gaps, and gcd-scaled predecessor overshoot are connected by exact identities and equivalences; cofinal supplies of the named witnesses imply that 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. Checked fixtures show that safe brackets with numerator monotonicity and a factor-11 predecessor rule are not inductive. No cofinal witness supply is proved, so neither half-membership nor universal Erdős #257 follows.

nodes.label: Explicit basis of the dyadic totient kernel span
nodes.statement: Lean constructs an explicit odd-core-indexed basis of the rational span of the full dyadic totient kernel, with exact span equality and linear independence. This is an independent constructive proof route; its infinite-dimensionality consequence is not an independent contribution because Coons's non-2-regularity theorem already implies it.

nodes.label: Dyadic totient-kernel finite-level rank
nodes.statement: For every e, a CRT–Dirichlet construction produces a separated nonzero evaluation minor for the canonical dyadic totient-kernel family, which is linearly independent with exact span dimension 2^e + 1. The same Lean development proves that the full dyadic kernel span is not finite-dimensional, but that corollary is not an independent contribution: it is equivalent, for this integer-valued sequence module, to Coons's non-2-regularity theorem. Even residues reduce to odd-core channels, and the compressed-adjoint boundary remains available. These coefficient-side theorems do not prove that S is irrational.

nodes.label: The Erdős–Borwein constant E is irrational
nodes.statement: E = ∑_{n≥1} 1/(2ⁿ − 1) is irrational, as the base-2 corollary of the full-support theorem.

nodes.label: Full-support Erdős–Borwein irrationality, every integer base b ≥ 2
nodes.statement: For every integer b ≥ 2, the series ∑_{n≥1} 1/(bⁿ − 1) is irrational (Erdős, 1948).

nodes.label: Erdős #249: irrationality of S = ∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ
nodes.statement: Not proved by this release. The reductions convert it into the unboundedness of the certificate supply, which is untouched.

nodes.label: Fatal-gap and eventual-right seam classification
nodes.statement: The concrete seam is eventually right when some S >= 5 makes every later seam word append true. A finite prefix u through rank d is a fatal half gap when V(u) + T_(d+1) < 1/2 < V(u) + w_(d+1), which makes every continuation miss 1/2. Eventual rightness is equivalent to the existence of such a gap, to nonmembership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set, and to a final skipped exponent in the real greedy orbit. This exact classification does not decide which branch holds.

nodes.label: Upper and first middle producers cannot feed an all-right tail
nodes.statement: At a putative last false rank D ≥ 13, the upper producer is impossible unconditionally. On the middle branch, let u be the finite support below D and B_D = u union {n : n > D} the lazy support that skips D and selects every later rank. Its value is V(u) + T_D < 1/2, while the exact carry swap sends transition carry C_D to centred carry C_D + 3 at row 2D+1. Thus C_D = -3 gives centred carry zero; the next coefficient rows have at least one and two forced divisors and make the carry negative by row 2D+3, contradicting finite-level nonnegativity below 1/2. This removes the upper branch and one middle cell, not the right-tail branch or the remaining cells -2 and -1.

nodes.label: Rank-26 phase sieve for the final middle -2 cell
nodes.statement: For every seam row s ≥ 27, the greedy decisions through rank 26 select exactly ranks 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 20, 21, and 26. Consequently, in a hypothetical final middle -2 cell at rank D ≥ 27 followed by an all-right suffix, D mod 21 lies in {11, 14, 17, 20}, D mod 10 is not 8, the mod-10 class 7 cannot pair with the mod-21 class 11, D mod 13 is not 11, and the mod-13 class 10 cannot pair with the mod-21 class 11. Exactly 412 of the 2730 joint residue classes survive. This is a finite necessary condition, not an exclusion; even a later survivor density tending to zero would not suffice without finite extinction or an Archimedean contradiction. The -1 and right-tail branches remain open.

nodes.label: First-harmonic gap implies a finite certificate
nodes.statement: Under the explicit dyadic room inequality, a constant-saving first-harmonic bound on one block, or on any nonempty finite set of indices below its right endpoint, forces a certified non-integrality witness in that set. No cofinal harmonic estimate is asserted.

nodes.label: Complex first-harmonic pivot decomposition
nodes.statement: For each positive cofactor m at most sqrt(X)/2, the canonical supplier fibre is exactly the injective image of the primes p in the shifted product interval under N = mp - (L-s+1). This exact bijection does not make a supplier prime globally isolated: at X=16, L=20, s=1, m=2, N=18 the pivot is 38=2*19, while the same prime 19 divides the distinct window argument N+1=19. Removing the pivot phase gives an exact decomposition of the block first-harmonic sum into a centred supplier-fibre correlation, a supplier-fibre mean term, a bad-supplier term, and a non-supplier term. At a positive scale satisfying the explicit dyadic-room inequality, if the real part of the centred term is at most 14X/25 and the other three norms are at most X/100, X/100, and 8X/25, then the real first-harmonic sum is at most 9X/10 and yields a finite certificate. A cofinal supply of these budgets implies irrationality of S. No global supplier-prime isolation, prime-distribution estimate, or decorrelation estimate supplying the budgets is proved.

nodes.label: Fixed-coefficient rewind contraction
nodes.statement: For coefficient c, the canonical inverse parent is T_c(k) = ceil((k+c)/2). For a length-L coefficient list with accumulated offset O, the iterated rewind is R(k) = floor((k+O)/2^L), with phase theta = (1+O) mod 2^L. If 1 <= B <= 2^L, all targets in [1,B] have one ancestor exactly when theta + B - 1 < 2^L; otherwise the endpoint ancestors differ by one and every target maps to one of that adjacent pair. The width bound does not exclude the seam-pair alternative or prove half-membership.

nodes.label: Fixed-precision valuation-unit no-go theorem
nodes.statement: At every fixed positive precision, each finite compatible valuation-unit word has a prefix-locked centred completion. Bounded local signatures alone therefore cannot exclude all finite centred endpoints; growing precision or global information remains possible.

nodes.label: Fixed-tail survival equivalence at every actual skip
nodes.statement: Writing r_M(1/2) for the residual after ranks through M and T_M for the complete tail after M, an actual skip M is final exactly when T_M < r_M(1/2). Negating the existence of a final skip yields r_M(1/2) <= T_M at every actual skip; together with the no-final-skip classification, this is equivalent to membership of 1/2. The required inequalities along the actual greedy orbit are not proved.

nodes.label: Affine three-scale frontier for the flexible odd window
nodes.statement: Under the stated short-correction bounds, the three half-word central-band predicates are exactly a three-scale affine escape disjunction. A uniform correction envelope alone cannot force that escape, as a zero-start affine orbit remains inside every scaled edge tube. Thus arithmetic state-correction correlation remains required.

nodes.label: Flexible three-rank odd-window reduction
nodes.statement: At an analytically admissible odd power-of-two rank, centrality in any one of the canonical odd rank or its next two base-four successors supplies the existing adjacent-suffix gap interface and hence irrationality. The remaining assertion is a cofinal three-rank band supply; no such supply is proved.

nodes.label: Fresh-prime endpoint-deficit decomposition
nodes.statement: At each positive height, every old-prime endpoint mass dominates the actual totient. The diagonal increment and literal foreign channel split exactly into the old Möbius increment and lower-minus-upper endpoint fresh deficits. The second and five-point curvature operators retain this split, and the nonnegative deficits bound the exact adverse weighted loss from the old-prime curvature margins. No cofinal deficit bound or irrationality conclusion is proved.

nodes.label: Greedy geometry of the Mersenne achievement set
nodes.statement: The Mersenne achievement set is compact, perfect, totally disconnected, nowhere dense, and has Lebesgue measure one. Membership is equivalent to greedy survival at every level; for the target 1/2 it is exactly equivalent to the canonical greedy orbit omitting infinitely many exponents. No finite normalized support has value 1/2, so positive membership would automatically produce an infinite rational-valued support and refute universal #257. Finite exact-rational death certificates soundly prove non-membership (3/4 is excluded at level one). The strict-tail Cantor geometry is recorded by Kovač–Tao; no novelty claim is made for the formalised refinements.

nodes.label: Half-carry reachability and compactness
nodes.statement: At an unresolved even seam, the scalar transition reaches exactly every integer terminal carry other than the one value 2*δ-c. If canonical seam coordinates are supplied at every sufficiently large even depth, then admissible finite half-carry words occur cofinally; compactness yields an infinite support A with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1/2. The canonical seam-supply hypothesis is not proved.

nodes.label: Finite shadows of the half cylinder
nodes.statement: For an admissible depth-N half-carry word with support A, terminal carry K_N, and future tail T_N, the residual is exactly 1/2 - X_A = (K_N - T_N)/2^N. At a first even seam the sole missing carry is H = 2 delta - c, so the integer strip [1,B] is fully reachable exactly when H lies outside it. The rank-three fixture A = {2,3} has residual 1/42 < 1/32 but its depth-six strip [1,8] contains H = 3, so raw dyadic safety does not force seam escape. The sole conditional membership input is the unproved governed frozen-margin producer, which requires future coefficient rows to cover the centred carry within J <= k+1 after every skipped rank k+1.

nodes.label: Half-divisor unit coefficient drop at the feedback row
nodes.statement: At the doubled feedback row, switching only the terminal half-divisor bit from false to true changes the support coefficient from C to C+1 and, under K' = 2K-C, drops the successor carry by exactly one. The same identity holds for any explicitly identified adjacent boundary pair, and the rewind adapter transfers such a shared-cutoff pair to the next protected seam while retaining the unit-drop witness. This does not construct such pairs globally.

nodes.label: Exact band localization of the final skip between two takes
nodes.statement: Suppose a take at rank b is followed by the next take at c > b+1, put q = 2^b − 1 and m = 2^(c−1), and write the pre-take residual as 1/R with 0 < R < q. The final intervening skip is dyadically unsafe exactly when q(m−1)/(q+m−1) < R < qm/(q+m), an interval of exact width q^2/((q+m)(q+m−1)). For one intervening skip this specializes to the two-thirds band (q(2q+1)/(3q+1), 2q(q+1)/(3q+2)), whose width is below 1/9; integral reciprocals never lie there, and the corresponding positive odd numerator is at least 7. These are local constraints: no theorem here says that the actual greedy orbit for 1/2 avoids a band or identifies the surviving last-producer cells with unsafe skips.

nodes.label: Positive half-membership classification in seam coordinates
nodes.statement: Membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set is equivalent to false successor terminal bits beyond every bound, to a cofinal sequence of such bits, and to a cofinal integer-seam sequence whose skipped ranks tend to infinity. These equivalences do not establish that any positive producer exists.

nodes.label: Exact rational second-channel reduction for the target one half
nodes.statement: A decidable rational separation predicate controls the greedy Mersenne orbit for the target 1/2. Lean verifies levels 1 through 6 exactly; proving the predicate for every n >= 7 would place 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set, equivalently would force infinitely many canonical greedy skips. The universal tail statement remains open.

nodes.label: Half-trapping reverse-carry interface
nodes.statement: Scalar-relation-invariant rational-linear channels have no nontrivial square determinant at any rank. Separately, a common coefficient word with a 1/0 seam and a common following overlap forces the terminal reverse-carry difference to be a power of two times an odd integer; a common nonnegative real carry bound yields the corresponding dyadic spacing inequality. The module neither supplies reverse-carry presentations nor a predecessor overlap, so it is not a greedy separation or irrationality theorem.

nodes.label: Integer-greedy first-wrap reduction
nodes.statement: For every s >= 3, let C_s = 2^(2s-1) - 2^s, let B_s = 2 floor(sqrt(2s)) + 4, and let r_s be the remainder obtained by greedily subtracting each descending truncated seam weight from C_s whenever possible. Each weight exceeds its complete tail by at least 2^(s+1) > B_s. Hence a positive subset-sum defect at most B_s exists exactly when 1 <= r_s <= B_s. The downstream skipped-seam escape hypothesis requires B_s < r_s at every genuine skipped rank. That hypothesis is not proved, so Erdős #257 remains open.

nodes.label: Largest skipped-rank gap and successor propagation
nodes.statement: At row s, let d be the largest skipped rank, u the selected prefix below d, L the integer weight of u together with the filled suffix above d, and U the weight obtained by replacing that suffix with d. In the late range d > 2s/3, equivalently 2s < 3d, Lean proves 3L + (3*2^(s+1) + 2*4^(s-d) + 4) = 3U. Upper or middle successors make the new terminal rank s the largest skip, while right successors preserve d. The global statement forcing an upper or middle step when 2(s+1) < 3d first fails is not proved.

nodes.label: Largest-skip induction from a quantified first-crossing hypothesis
nodes.statement: Assume that for every s >= 14 and largest skip d with 2s < 3d, either 2(s+1) < 3d or the transition to row s+1 is upper or middle. Lean checks the base s = 14, d = 13 with 28 < 39. Under the hypothesis, induction gives a largest skip beyond two thirds at every row s >= 14; these skipped ranks tend to infinity, so 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. The universal next-row hypothesis is not proved.

nodes.label: Last-producer tail-escape reduction
nodes.statement: If every actual middle transition at D ≥ 13 other than the discharged cell C_D = -3 satisfies Theta_D < C_D, then an eventual right seam is impossible and 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. Since Theta_D ≥ 0, this leaves two open inputs: exclude C_D = -2,-1 and prove Theta_D < C_D at every remaining transition with C_D ≥ 0. A square-root producer lower bound is a separate sufficient hypothesis. None of these arithmetic inputs is proved.

nodes.label: LCM factor-ideal anchor-pulse no-go theorem
nodes.statement: For every t ≥ 3, a nonzero synthetic affine carry has forcing letters in the principal ideal generated by φ(lcm(1,…,t)), matches every stated whole-ray anchor, and remains within the diagonal bounds while its state is a strict survivor. The same countermodel survives every finite integer shift polynomial. Thus factor ideals, whole-ray anchors, and finite-rank shift algebra alone do not force carry escape. The construction does not assert that its forcing letters are actual totient differences and does not rule out nonlinear use of fresh divisor channels.

nodes.label: Localized protected seam compactness
nodes.statement: At depth M, realized localized seam means only the forward implication: every seam-reachable carry k in [3,27] is the terminal carry of an admissible finite word. The seam's unique hole is H = 2 delta - c, so choosing k = 4 when H = 3 and k = 3 otherwise supplies one admissible word. If such realizations occur cofinally, then cofinal admissibility and an infinite support A with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1/2 follow. The cofinal realization supply is not proved, so Erdős #257 remains open.

nodes.label: The Mersenne–Lambert ladder identities
nodes.statement: L(μ) = 1/2, L(φ) = 2, L(φ*μ) = S, and the Möbius-square lens S = 1/2 + ∑ μ(d)/(2^d − 1)², placing the open constant one convolution from the machine-checked irrational E.

nodes.label: Exact Mersenne-shadow denominator and survivor bounds
nodes.statement: The reduced denominator of the lcm-height scaled Möbius shadow is computed exactly at every height, and for t ≥ 5 an explicit upper-half Mersenne product both divides it and supplies a quantitative lower bound.

nodes.label: Finite Mersenne tail-atom determinant boundary
nodes.statement: A periodic Mersenne tail atom has the exact doubling-and-wrap carry law. For any finite atom matrix, clearing the product of its column Mersenne denominators yields the integral numerator determinant; a nonzero cleared weighted minor therefore has absolute value at least one. This is a finite-denominator boundary for an atom-minor route, not an irrationality criterion for S.

nodes.label: Finite-prefix middle-producer cardinality reduction
nodes.statement: Put g_D = #G_D. The augmented finite support A_D = G_D union {D} has g_D + 1 elements, so its complete future divisor-incidence tail satisfies Theta_D ≤ g_D + 1. Since C_D = 4 R_(D,D) - P_D - 4, the inequality g_D + P_D + 5 < 4 R_(D,D) is exactly g_D + 1 < C_D; required at every late middle transition, it excludes the negative cells and proves tail dominance, hence half-membership. The stronger row-scale hypothesis R_(D,D) ≥ D also suffices. Neither hypothesis is proved.

nodes.label: Mixed cofinal half-carry fan-in
nodes.statement: For every N, suppose there is M >= N carrying either a selected protected half-carry window or a localized realized one-hole seam. The window branch chooses carry 1; the seam branch chooses 4 when its unique hole is 3 and 3 otherwise. Either branch supplies one admissible finite word, and the branches may alternate with N. Hence cofinal admissibility and, by compactness, an infinite support A with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1/2 follow. This mixed cofinal hypothesis is not proved, so Erdős #257 remains open.

nodes.label: Mixed prime-power support-layer identity
nodes.statement: Exact p-adic and q-adic coefficient-layer operators commute. For distinct primes and a residual argument coprime to their product, the two-layer operator on the support coefficient equals the iterated exact-prime-power pullback. The checked singleton {12} fixture has mixed (2²,3) layer value one at residual argument one. This is finite coefficient algebra only, with no decimation transport, bounded-Ω endpoint, or irrationality theorem.

nodes.label: Möbius-sign support one-half no-go
nodes.statement: The Boolean support selected by the negative Möbius values has sum 1/2 plus the positive Möbius tail and is therefore at least 1/2 + 1/63. This closes the sign-truncation route to the target value 1/2; it does not exclude another infinite Boolean support with that value.

nodes.label: Conditional orthogonal-petal sunflower reduction
nodes.statement: For a finite-core orthogonal-petal bouquet at base 2, the exact uniform tail-selection predicate implies a forced-carry certificate supply and hence irrationality of the associated support series. Lean formalises the carry conversion and an explicit infinite alternating-core, squared-prime-petal bouquet whose elements have three prime factors with multiplicity. The tail-selection predicate itself is not proved, so this does not add an unconditional #257 support family.

nodes.label: Parity obstruction for the reduced margin socket
nodes.statement: For every positive even modulus and every radius in the stated nontrivial range, each parity class contains both a reduced-margin-socket hit and a miss. The same holds for a positive power-of-two modulus. Thus quotient parity alone cannot decide the reduced signed-margin socket. No t = 827 numeral or signed-margin certificate is asserted.

nodes.label: Period-four signed residue-selection obstruction
nodes.statement: For the period-four signed weight 1,0,−1,0, the associated signed divisor coefficient vanishes for every n congruent to 3 modulo 4. A whole arithmetic progression can therefore carry zero coefficient, so residue-blind selection cannot force a protected nonzero residue for every periodic signed weight.

nodes.label: Eventually-periodic nonnegative weighted Lambert irrationality
nodes.statement: For every integer base b ≥ 2, an eventually-periodic nonnegative rational coefficient sequence with a positive value at a positive index in its periodic region has irrational series ∑ γ(a)/(b^a − 1). This includes eventually-periodic natural-number weights and indicator supports. Luca–Tachiya prove a broader periodic rational-coefficient theorem by different methods; no priority claim is made here.

nodes.label: Periodic signed-weight irrational-or-terminating dichotomy
nodes.statement: For every integer base b ≥ 2 and every periodic integer weight w, the signed series ∑ w(a)/(b^a − 1) is irrational or some power of b times its value is an integer. Excluding that terminating alternative implies irrationality. The terminating alternative is not excluded in general, so the full mixed-sign periodic-coefficient theorem is not claimed.

nodes.label: Pivot anti-reconstruction and window-pair reduction
nodes.statement: On a finite supplier fibre, sufficient counted phase-pair separation feeds a certified non-integrality witness through exact reconstruction-defect and variance identities. Cofinal pivot anti-reconstruction, reconstruction variance, or counted-pair producers imply irrationality of S. The fibre-free cofinal window-pair predicate is exactly equivalent to irrationality of S. No cofinal arithmetic producer is proved.

nodes.label: Exact power-of-two one-bit lift
nodes.statement: Given agreement modulo 2^k, agreement modulo 2^(k+1) is exactly evenness of the signed quotient after division by 2^k; failure gives the unique offset class. In particular, a signed difference 16*c agrees modulo 32 exactly when c is even. Under the stated correction and margin budget, the centered signed-margin socket is exactly failure of this next lift. This provides a finite fifth-bit interface and does not supply cofactor parity at unbounded scales.

nodes.label: Irrationality of the prime-support series ∑_p 1/(2^p − 1)
nodes.statement: Tao–Teräväinen; settles the prime-support special case of #257. Only the identity bridge to ∑ ω(n)/2ⁿ is formalised, not the irrationality.

nodes.label: Primitive Euler-coordinate finite-jet obstruction
nodes.statement: For the primitive-conductor weight A = φ*μ, every positive index clearing the normalized coordinates A(n)/n through horizon N is divisible by the two-tier primorial: 4 at the prime 2 once N ≥ 4, p² for odd p with p² ≤ N, and p otherwise. Hence no fixed positive index clears all normalized coordinates. This is a finite Euler/Witt-coordinate obstruction only; it gives no irrationality criterion for S.

nodes.label: Prime-power reduced-denominator unit-gap ceiling
nodes.statement: For the reduced-denominator unit-gap predicate at an odd prime power p^e, the candidate interval is empty or has exactly one candidate divisible by p; in particular its count is at most one. The exact row (u,N,K) = (3,3,5) satisfies the unit-gap predicate while the corresponding ordinary empty-gap inequality fails. This is a finite certificate-level strengthening, not an unbounded supply theorem or an irrationality criterion for S.

nodes.label: Exact producer-carry residual and sign criteria
nodes.statement: For A contained in {2,...,d}, let f_A(n) count support divisors, let C_(A,d) be the affine integer state after 2d+1 updates from 1, and let Theta_(A,d) be the complete scaled coefficient tail after depth 2d+2. Then 1/2 - X_A = 2^(-(2d+2))(C_(A,d) - Theta_(A,d)). Hence C_(A,d) > Theta_(A,d) iff X_A < 1/2 and C_(A,d) < Theta_(A,d) iff X_A > 1/2; a negative carry is sufficient for the latter because the tail is nonnegative, and carry at most -8 gives a full Mersenne-gap margin. No occurrence theorem for these carries is proved.

nodes.label: Exact quarter-band failure cells for adjacent seam cuts
nodes.statement: At row s put H = 2^(s-1), and let R, U, R', p^-, p^+ be the adjacent cut's remainder, overshoot, next remainder, below pulse, and above pulse. On the non-carry middle branch, failure R' >= 8H is equivalent to the unique cell R = H+k with p^- <= 4k < p^-+4. On the terminal-reset branch, failure is equivalent to R = 3H+k with p^-+4 <= 4k and 4k+16H < 4(R+U)+p^+. These are exact failure classifications, not an avoidance theorem for the concrete seam orbit.

nodes.label: Realized rewind phase identity
nodes.statement: For a realized carry-one fixed-coefficient history, list the suffix bits newest row first and let X be their binary numeral, so the newest bit has weight 2^0. If D = 2^L, the rewind phase is exactly theta = D - 1 - X. The interval [1,B] rewinds to one ancestor exactly when B - 1 <= X; equivalently, for the frozen-prefix carry Z = 1 + X, exactly when B <= Z. No theorem proves either coverage inequality at all sufficiently large depths.

nodes.label: Rationality-forced reciprocal-mass lower bound
nodes.statement: A rational support-series value with odd denominator part v forces reciprocal mass at least 1/ord_v(2), or divergence; an infinite support with dyadic-rational value has reciprocal mass divergent or greater than one.

nodes.label: Exact right-branch window and reset-deficit escape law
nodes.statement: Write R_s for the final integer-greedy remainder and p_s^- for the below pulse. At a largest skip d with 2s < 3d, a right branch forces 2^(s+1)+4 <= 4R_s and 12R_s+3*2^(s+1) < 4*(3*2^(s+1)+2*4^(s-d)+4)+6(s-2), and it satisfies R_(s+1)+2^(s+1)+p_s^-+4 = 4R_s. If R_s <= 2^s and delta_s = 2^s-R_s, every further right step gives delta_(s+1) >= 4 delta_s while the reference scale doubles; hence 2^s <= 2^k delta_s forces an upper-or-middle row t in [s,s+k]. The global anti-concentration needed to exclude the pinned interval along the actual orbit is not proved.

nodes.label: Residual-gauge obstruction for monomial minors
nodes.statement: For a residual-weighted monomial matrix, common nonzero residual weights act by a right diagonal gauge and preserve determinant nonvanishing. Under the locked inverse-phase gauge, an exponent-one row is identically 1 even when the determinant remains nonzero; allowing row-dependent residuals reconstructs a consecutive-power matrix with zeroth row identically 1. Thus residual-blind rank, determinant, and conditioning criteria alone cannot exclude the target. This does not rule out a criterion with an additional arithmetic coupling identity, and it gives no irrationality criterion.

nodes.label: Finite rewind boundary-pair obstruction
nodes.statement: A concrete depth-26 selected two-word window has a depth-27 explicit rewind step with history [1], a width-two numerical seam, and the doubled-row identity, but no depth-13 half-divisor boundary-pair witness. Therefore scalar one-row seam data alone does not entail the structural boundary predicate required by the cofinal consumer.

nodes.label: Operational bridge from rewind seams to protected next-row seams
nodes.statement: Let W = (a^h)_(1 <= h <= R) be a selected depth-N window whose targets rewind to two adjacent base words at depth M. If D and phi are the rewind denominator and phase, delta = D-phi, M <= N, (N+1)/2 <= M, R <= D, and the adjacent base words have row-(N+1) coefficients c+1 and c, then f_(a^h)(N+1) equals c+1 for h <= delta and c for h > delta. If 27 <= S <= 2 floor(sqrt(N+1))+4 and S+c+1 <= 2R, the profile realizes a protected one-hole seam at row N+1. The rewind provenance, seam pair, coefficient drop, strip, and buffer are inputs. For a full half-strip window the divisor bound supplies the buffer, but the coefficient drop remains unproved.

nodes.label: Exact seam-hole to producer-carry alignment identity
nodes.statement: Let P omit s, put A = P union {s}, and let delta be the half-carry of A at row 2s-2. Define the first-wrap hole H = 2 delta - f_P(2s) and paired incidence pulse Pi = 2 f_A(2s+1) + f_A(2s+2). Then the producer carry is exactly C(A,s) = 4(H-1) - Pi. This aligns the seam and producer coordinates but supplies no sign, size, or occurrence estimate.

nodes.label: Selected half-carry windows
nodes.statement: A selected half-carry window at depth N and radius R assigns every k in [1,R] an admissible Boolean word of depth N whose terminal carry is k. If such windows exist at every sufficiently large depth with R >= 1, their k = 1 representatives give cofinal finite admissibility; compactness then yields an infinite support A with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1/2. The unproved object-level input is a coherent one-row history: either all representatives agree on membership of every divisor of N+1, making their next coefficient common, or the adjacent outcome realizes the canonical one-hole seam. The module supplies no such cofinal history.

nodes.label: Conditional suffix-cylinder feedback and child-gap recurrence
nodes.statement: For the depth-18 selected window, the common depth-13 prefix and suffix numeral satisfy ν + k = 17. Under a common next coefficient C the endpoint obeys E' = 2E - C. At a feedback row the full cylinder either advances or leaves one carry gap [g_-,g_+]. If the lower and upper families have coefficients C_- and C_+ and satisfy the explicit positivity, ordering, strip, and buffer inequalities, the next gap is exactly [2g_- - C_- - 1, 2g_+ - C_+]. Cutoff promotion appends forced bits 0 and 1 and preserves consecutive prefixes. A swallowed two-row update forces the sharp quarter-band bound B <= 4(g_+ - g_- + 1) + 2. Cofinal full stages would produce an infinite support of value 1/2, but no such cofinal family or uniform coefficient inequalities are proved.

nodes.label: Verified finite suffix-cylinder stages through depth 52
nodes.statement: A common depth-13 prefix supports full selected windows at every depth 18 through 27, and the threshold continuation reaches depth 29 while covering the protected strip. At depth 29, cutoffs 14 through 25 remain common and cutoff 26 does not. A separate exact recurrence reaches depth 51 with endpoint 51,327,745 beyond the next head threshold, and the promoted depth-52 successor supplies a terminal-strip witness. These are finite stages, not an unbounded induction.

nodes.label: Computed depth-18 selected half-carry window base
nodes.statement: A kernel-reflected Boolean table supplies a selected half-carry window at depth 18 for every terminal carry in the half strip [1,12]. The representatives share a common depth-13 restriction, yielding the first next-row divisor-agreement certificate. This is a finite base and does not construct selected windows at unbounded depths.

nodes.label: Transcendence of ∑ σ(m)/2^m
nodes.statement: Nesterenko (1996); the ladder rung L(Id). Cited for positioning, not formalised here.

nodes.label: Signed dyadic-moment algebra
nodes.statement: A rectangular determinant expansion over all maps and a unique-largest-dyadic-exponent parity lemma are formalised. The latter makes a cleared finite dyadic sum odd, hence nonzero, when its selected numerator is odd and its exponent is strictly largest. This is finite algebraic substrate only: it proves neither non-vanishing of the actual totient Hankel determinants nor an irrationality criterion.

nodes.label: Square-CRT correction suppression
nodes.statement: For every finite family of distinct primes and prescribed anchors, a bounded simultaneous square-CRT base removes the prime-dilation correction at every admissible finite shift. Checked clean cubes can have vanishing coefficients and can also have a nonzero coefficient; this finite mechanism supplies neither an unbounded certificate family nor an irrationality criterion for the totient constant.

nodes.label: Squared-Lambert identities for divisor count and the first gcd moment
nodes.statement: The squared-Mersenne Lambert series with weight 1 equals the base-1/2 series of sigma(n)-tau(n), and the series with weight phi equals the base-1/2 series of P(n)-n, where P is Pillai's gcd-sum function. These are the exact divisor-count and first-moment identities for the fair-coin gcd law; the separately cited irrationality of the constant-weight value is not claimed as formalised here.

nodes.label: Sharp squared-Mersenne diagonal enclosure
nodes.statement: The scaled diagonal tail difference is written as an explicit Lambert-projected centre plus a signed squared-Mersenne tail, with a sharp symmetric bound and a checked separation criterion for missing the full target.

nodes.label: Irrationality of the base-2 squarefree-support series
nodes.statement: Duverney–Tachiya Corollary 1.2 and Example 1.1 prove linear independence of 1 and the squarefree Lambert sum including n=1; subtracting that rational term settles the support {n≥2:n squarefree} at base 2. Their condition |q|^L≤s does not cover the same support at integer bases b≥3. This result is not formalised here.

nodes.label: Reduced-direction normalization and Stern–Brocot cylinder law
nodes.statement: The Mersenne weights of positive reduced slopes sum exactly to one. At every positive Stern–Brocot node (a,b), the cylinder mass 1/((2^a-1)(2^b-1)) splits into its stop mass and two child cylinders; the depth-d unfolding has error between zero and (2/3)^d times the cylinder mass and converges to the closed form.

nodes.label: Fibonacci and continuant stability of Stern–Brocot runs
nodes.statement: A Stern–Brocot word with r nonempty alternating runs has height at least F_(r+3), with equality on the all-unit run spine. Writing each run length as 1+e_i gives an exact multiaffine continuant-defect expansion, the sharp global gain F_(r+1) sum e_i, and exact one-site coefficient F_(i+2)F_(r-i+1). Under the gcd-one weight 2^-(a+b), the first induced run layer has mass 1/2, while the natural denominator-bookkeeping exponent is exactly F_(r+3)-2. These are source-level combinatorial and arithmetic facts; no analytic denominator survival or irrationality conclusion is claimed.

nodes.label: Sublogarithmic divisor-coverage zero windows
nodes.statement: A rational support-series value forces every zero window in the divisor-count coefficient to have length at most ε·log₂(N+1) + B, where B ≥ 0 is built from ε, c and v but is bound after the support and numerator, so no single constant is claimed uniform across supports. This constrains coverage; it does not solve universal #257.

nodes.label: Named infinite-support irrationality families toward #257
nodes.statement: For every base b ≥ 2, ∑_{n∈A} 1/(bⁿ − 1) is irrational for factorial support, power-of-two support, multiples, pairwise-coprime supports with summable reciprocals, eventually-periodic supports, residue classes, and the odd numbers. Proved families, not the universal statement.

nodes.label: Tempered tail-orbit rigidity criterion
nodes.statement: For coefficients c(n) ≤ n, the binary series ∑ c(n)/2ⁿ is rational exactly when a tempered integer carry orbit exists, and every tempered orbit equals the scaled tail.

nodes.label: Terminal-only cofinal square-root-strip closure
nodes.statement: A normalized finite word with terminal half carry in the square-root strip has support-series value within (4M+12)/2^M of 1/2. Thus cofinally many such terminal-only witnesses, with neither coherent histories nor earlier-row bounds, force 1/2 into the Mersenne achievement set and yield an infinite support with support-series value 1/2. The cofinal terminal-witness supply is not proved.

nodes.label: Scaled terminal-vanishing closure
nodes.statement: A normalized sequence of finite terminal words whose depths tend to infinity and whose terminal carries divided by the corresponding powers of 2 tend to zero has support-series values converging to 1/2. Closedness of the Mersenne achievement set then gives membership of 1/2 and an infinite support with that value. The prior cofinal square-root-strip condition maps into this weaker socket, but no scaled-vanishing sequence is constructed.

nodes.label: Unconditional carry-kernel anti-compression
nodes.statement: If the totient coefficient series were rational, one positive-multiplier tempered integral carry would have canonical carry-section span dimension at least 2^e − 1 for every e. The all-level kernel-independence producer is supplied by the CRT–Dirichlet minor theorem. No finite-rank bound for every rationality-supplied carry is proved, so this is an infinite anti-compression barrier rather than an irrationality criterion for S.

nodes.label: Fair-coin coprimality form of the totient constant
nodes.statement: For independent fair-coin geometric waiting times X and Y on the positive integers, S = 1/2 + P(gcd(X,Y)=1), where the probability is the visible coprime-pair series. That probability has no rational representation with denominator at most 39819823323350687661677887437915526. This is an exact reformulation and quantitative corollary; irrationality remains open.

nodes.label: Verified transport-window certificates
nodes.statement: Lean verifies the sharp prime-jump certificate at (H,p,L)=(12,5,15) and the balanced three-transport certificate at (H,L)=(60,12). These bounded instances do not establish any unbounded supply.

nodes.label: Transport and curvature reductions for Erdős #249
nodes.statement: Curvature, fixed-three exponent transport, anchored (3,5) transport, prime-jump, and balanced three-transport observables each have exact finite non-integrality consumers whose unbounded supply would imply irrationality of the totient constant. Every supply hypothesis remains open.

nodes.label: Canonical quotient-greedy and scaled-remainder frontier at 1/21
nodes.statement: Membership of 1/21 in the Mersenne achievement set is equivalent both to excluding one explicit fatal/cofinite/aligned branch and to cofinally bounded scaled actual greedy remainders. Every closed Boolean quotient row is the deterministic quotient-greedy row; any unbounded sequence of canonical rows with remainder at most 2^R gives membership. On the complementary fatal branch the remainder is eventually strictly supercapacity, the boundary rank is always selected, and support and remainder follow one exact affine recurrence. A final skipped exponent also forces a structured one-sided approximation to the Erdős–Borwein constant with exact denominator-order constraints. These results isolate permanent affine supercapacity as the surviving late regime; they do not contradict it or prove 1/21 membership.

nodes.label: Carry states are unbounded over infinite rational-valued supports
nodes.statement: An infinite support with rational series value has an unbounded positive carry state, closing finite-state readings of the carry system.

nodes.label: Erdős #257, universal form
nodes.statement: Irrationality of ∑_{n∈A} 1/(2ⁿ − 1) for every infinite A is not proved by this release; only named families are formalised.

nodes.label: Upper-reset dyadic-band certificates through row 30
nodes.statement: At an upper transition G_(d+1) = H_d, put Q_d = 4 O_d + A_d from the upper overshoot and divisor pulse and B_(d,j) = 2^(d-j+1). For every 13 <= d <= 30 and j <= d, Lean proves B_(d,j) < Q_d or Q_d + 2(d+j) <= B_(d,j), equivalently avoidance of Q_d <= B_(d,j) < Q_d + 2(d+j). For fixed d, one exact successor remainder R_(d+1,d+1) certifies every j. This is bounded evidence and proves no global upper-reset band-escape hypothesis.

nodes.label: Short connections inside polynomial lemniscates
nodes.question: For a monic polynomial whose roots lie in the open unit disc, must two roots be joinable by a curve of length less than two inside the open unit lemniscate?

nodes.label: Lambert-type series at rational bases
nodes.question: For which rational bases is the corresponding series irrational? The smallest resistant explicit base is three halves.

nodes.label: Reciprocal-tail rigidity near the Sylvester recurrence
nodes.question: Under a rapid-growth hypothesis on an integer sequence, does rationality of its reciprocal sum force the sequence to satisfy the Sylvester recurrence eventually?

nodes.label: The binary totient series
nodes.question: Is the binary Lambert series sum phi(n)/2^n irrational?

nodes.label: The prime-gap dyadic series
nodes.question: Is the dyadic series sum p_n/2^n over consecutive primes irrational? Equivalently, is the corresponding consecutive-prime-gap dyadic series irrational?

nodes.label: Reciprocal sums over infinite exponent supports
nodes.question: Is the sum of 1/(2^n-1) over every infinite set of positive exponents irrational?

nodes.label: Three-prime running least common multiples
nodes.question: For a finite set of at least two primes, is the sum of reciprocals of the running least common multiples of the smooth numbers irrational? This library treats the three-prime case.

nodes.label: The factorial-denominator series
nodes.question: Is the series sum_{n >= 2} 1/(n! - 1) irrational?

nodes.label: Finite totient-kernel rank review unit
nodes.boundary: Preparation is not Comparator replay, Palomar review, registration, or acceptance.

nodes.label: A bounded search records finite geometric evidence.
nodes.boundary: Finite evidence does not settle the universal problem.

nodes.label: The Newton value equation and its exponential first integral are checked exactly.
nodes.boundary: Value decay alone does not give a short connecting curve.

nodes.label: The paper identifies an invalid local saddle block in a claimed unrestricted proof.
nodes.boundary: The diagnosis does not prove that no repair exists.

nodes.label: Distinct positive rays exclude a finite Newton connection.
nodes.boundary: The result is a route obstruction, not the global theorem.

nodes.label: A quantified small constant perturbation keeps every polynomial root inside the open unit disc.
nodes.boundary: Root retention is one input to a still-incomplete route.

nodes.label: Collision translations are parameterised by real affine lines and an arbitrarily small common translation avoids finitely many of them.
nodes.boundary: The finite-family avoidance theorem does not perform the global topology or metric gluing.

nodes.label: The coordinatewise corridor forces a power-versus-linear inequality and cannot occur at base 3/2.
nodes.boundary: This excludes one proof architecture and proves no irrationality statement.

nodes.label: Endpoint residues at 2 and 3 exclude a common multiplier under unit-endpoint hypotheses.
nodes.boundary: Other local or cross-row arithmetic remains possible.

nodes.label: Binary selectors collide in the four-jet signature at the stated rank and depth.
nodes.boundary: A signed relation is not nonzero analytic data.

nodes.label: Exact height-region inclusions and exclusions, Padé denominator-exponent bounds, and a rectangular Hermite-Padé threshold no-go are checked.
nodes.boundary: The analytic remainder and nonvanishing input remain untreated.

nodes.label: The exact rational-base cleared-tail recurrence exposes exponential denominator-base forcing absent at integer bases.
nodes.boundary: The recurrence is not derived from a rationality contradiction.

nodes.label: Integer scalar content changes analytic error and exterior determinant by matching factors, yielding no margin by itself.
nodes.boundary: The conclusion is scoped to one normalisation strategy.

nodes.label: Irrationality at 7/2 is obtained from an external analytic criterion whose elementary height hypothesis is checked in Lean.
nodes.boundary: Comparator may check the height inequality, not the cited theorem application.

nodes.label: Normalised vanishing excludes a cofinally bounded negative part and forces eventual Sylvester behaviour.
nodes.boundary: Every positivity, dynamics, bounded-rise, and vanishing hypothesis remains explicit.

nodes.label: A bounded-rise sequence cannot remain coprime to fresh pairwise-coprime moduli; reduced tails inherit this obstruction.
nodes.boundary: The required bounded-rise input is not automatic for the original sequence.

nodes.label: Exact update and defect identities, scale equivariance, zero absorption, and eventual recovery of the Sylvester recurrence.
nodes.boundary: The recovery theorem requires eventual centred-state vanishing.

nodes.label: Finite normalised negative mass forces eventual zero and hence the Sylvester recurrence.
nodes.boundary: Summability of the negative mass is unproved for the original problem.

nodes.label: Constant, eventually constant, periodic, and eventually periodic negative-error orbits are excluded in their stated regimes.
nodes.boundary: The exclusions do not cover arbitrary unbounded negative behaviour.

nodes.label: Eventually periodic nonnegative rational weights give an irrational Lambert series.
nodes.boundary: The totient-derived weights are not eventually periodic.

nodes.label: Rationality forces a tempered integral tail orbit with unbounded finite-level carry rank.
nodes.boundary: This is a necessary consequence, not a contradiction.

nodes.label: Pointwise, cofinal, lcm-diagonal, and separated-window certificate supplies are exact or sufficient reformulations.
nodes.boundary: Equivalent producer statements are as hard as the unresolved target.

nodes.label: A Farey denominator exclusion through 7.96e34, sharp for its selected window, and diagonal certificates through t=82.
nodes.boundary: The selected finite window and certificate ceiling do not imply an unbounded producer.

nodes.label: For every base k at least 2, Lean checks the arithmetic reduction, exact nonmultiple-residue coordinates, unconditional canonical spanning, and exact rank k^e+1 conditional on canonical-family linear independence.
nodes.boundary: Lean does not prove all-base affine-section independence or formalise Martin's theorem. The unconditional basis and rank conclusions in the paper use that external input.

nodes.label: An explicit odd-core basis and relation normal form for the full dyadic totient kernel.
nodes.boundary: The basis theorem does not connect rationality of the series to finite kernel rank.

nodes.label: An independent constructive proof of exact finite-level dyadic rank 2^e+1, together with a kernel-checked full-kernel infinite-dimensionality corollary already implied by Coons's non-2-regularity theorem.
nodes.boundary: Only the finite-level rank is presented as an additional result; full-kernel infinite-dimensionality is prior-art context, and no rationality-to-finite-rank bridge is proved.

nodes.label: The totient series is rewritten as a Lambert series with explicit nonnegative, unbounded prime-power coefficients.
nodes.boundary: The coefficient identities do not prove irrationality.

nodes.label: Prime gaps are unbounded and non-eventually-periodic, while an explicit nonperiodic unbounded countermodel still has rational sum.
nodes.boundary: Comparator checks the exact theorem, not the broader methodological interpretation.

nodes.label: Block identities and exact denominator criteria classify rationality through integral positive tail shifts.
nodes.boundary: The concrete prime-gap producer remains missing.

nodes.label: Exact finite summation by parts, the unconditional infinite prime-gap identity, and irrationality equivalence.
nodes.boundary: The equivalence does not prove irrationality of either series.

nodes.label: Cofinal adjacent small mismatches would rule out eventual integral shifts for the prime-gap tail.
nodes.boundary: The cofinal mismatch producer is unproved.

nodes.label: Odd rational denominators give totient-length integral shifts, and integrality propagates through the recurrence.
nodes.boundary: This describes rational states and supplies no contradiction for actual prime gaps.

nodes.label: Compactness, perfectness, total disconnectedness, nowhere density, and measure one for the unrestricted achievement set.
nodes.boundary: Geometry of the full set does not decide irrationality of every coded point.

nodes.label: The multiplicative order of the base modulo a reduced finite-sum denominator is the support lcm, forcing denominator growth.
nodes.boundary: A finite-support denominator theorem does not settle an infinite-support sum.

nodes.label: Exact greedy characterisations and finite-support exclusions isolate the remaining 1/2 and 1/21 alternatives.
nodes.boundary: Neither membership question is decided.

nodes.label: Full, factorial, power-of-two, multiple, pairwise-coprime, eventually periodic, residue-class, and odd supports are formalised.
nodes.boundary: Structured known families do not cover arbitrary infinite supports.
